items.name: SRC_TAPS
items.doc: Taps per phase. 64 puts the design's transition band comfortably inside what a Kaiser of this beta can hold at every standard rate pair, and costs 64 multiply-adds per output sample — about 12 M flops per track-minute at 48 kHz, which is nothing offline.

items.name: SRC_STOPBAND_DB
items.doc: Stopband attenuation the window is designed for, in dB. 96 dB is below the noise floor of any take this console can capture (float capture of a 24-bit converter), so the conversion is not what limits the file.

items.name: SRC_ROLLOFF
items.doc: How much of the shared Nyquist the passband keeps. The remaining 8 % is the transition band the window needs to reach its stopband: at 48 kHz that puts the corner at 22.08 kHz and the stopband in place by 24 kHz.

items.name: SRC_MAX_L
items.doc: The largest interpolation factor a plan may carry. 44.1 kHz -> 192 kHz is 640/147, the widest pair the console's standard rates produce; the cap refuses an exotic pair before it allocates a table nobody budgeted for, rather than discovering it as a bad_alloc.
